name_note: GTDB treats Bifidobacterium longum as a single species, so genomes of the milk-adapted subspecies infantis fall under this name.

sentences.text: Bifidobacteria, the genus of Bifidobacterium longum, are Gram-positive prokaryotes that naturally colonise the human gastrointestinal tract and vagina and are regarded as key commensals.
Bioinformatic analysis of a 2.26-megabase genome from an infant-derived strain revealed physiological traits that could partly explain its adaptation to the colon.
After birth the breastfed infant gut is rapidly colonised by a community often dominated by bifidobacteria.
The subspecies infantis carries gene clusters for milk oligosaccharide use and is described as unusually able to consume any human milk oligosaccharide structure.
Individual strains have been trialled in people; strain 1714 was given to healthy volunteers to test effects on stress, cognition and brain activity.
